Biteganyijwe ko Minisitiri w'intebe w'Ubwongereza Andy Burnham aza kuvuga ko igihugu cye cyahombye byinshi kurusha ibyo cyungutse nyuma yo kuva mu muryango w'Ubumwe bw'Uburayi (EU), ibizwi nka Brexit, mu ijambo avuga kuri uyu wa mbere, mbere y'inama izahuza Ubwongereza n'uwo muryango izabera i Buruseli mu mpera y'iki cyumweru.

Mu ijambo ageza ku bitabiriye ibirori bibera i London (Lord Mayor's Banquet), Burnham aragereranya amasezerano Ubwongereza bwagiranye na EU nyuma ya Brexit n'ukuntu abantu bahuriza ku gushimagiza ikintu kandi babizi ko kitari cyo kubera ko badashaka kwitandukanya na benshi bagishyigikiye, avuga ko kuva muri uwo muryango mu buryo bwo kwitandukanya cyane n'ibigo byawo byashyizeho inzitizi ku bucuruzi, mu gihe isezerano ryo "kwisubiza ububasha bwo kwifatira ibyemezo" ritigeze rigerwaho.

Burnham arashaka kugirana amasezerano mashya n'uwo muryango ku bijyanye n'ibiribwa, ingufu n'urujya n'uruza rw'urubyiruko, mu nama iteganyijwe ku wa gatanu.

Burnham yavuze ko ayo masezerano ashobora kugirira impande zombi akamaro.

Ishyaka ry'abatsimbaraye ku bya kera(Conservateurs), ritavuga rumwe n'ubutegetsi mu Bwongereza, ryavuze ko ishyaka ry'abakozi (Labour), riri ku butegetsi, ririmo "kugarura Ubwongereza mu muryango w'Ubumwe bw'Uburayi rwihishwa, binyuze mu mavugurura y'imikoranire iteruye n'uwo muryango".

Biteganyijwe ko Burnham azavuga ati: "Bimeze nk'inkuru y'umwami wambaye ubusa, aho nta muntu n'umwe ushaka kuvuga ukuri kugaragarira buri wese. Jyewe ndavuga ibyo mbona. Mu by'ukuri, umwami nta cyo yambaye.

"Uburyo Brexit yashyizwe mu bikorwa ntibwatanze umusaruro. Twahombye byinshi kurusha ibyo twungutse."

Minisitiri w'Intebe w'intebe avuga ko ashaka kuvugurura umubano w'Ubwongereza n'umuryango w'Ubumwe bw'Uburayi. Ariko ashimangira ko atavuga ko icyemezo cyo kuva muri uwo muryango cyari kibi, ahubwo ko uburyo byakozwemo ari bwo bwari ikibazo.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Azavuga ko amasezerano ayo ari yo yose azagirana n'uwo muryango agomba gutsinda ikizamini yise "Makerfield test", kigamije kureba niba azana impinduka zifatika mu buzima bwa buri munsi bw'abaturage, kandi akagera ku rwego rwegereye ibyo abantu batekerezaga ko batoye mu matora ya kamarampaka yo mu 2016.

Burnham kandi ateganyijwe kongera gushimangira ko yubahiriza ibyo ishyaka ry'abakozi ryasezeranyije mu nyandiko yaryo y'ibyo rizakora mu gihe cy'imyaka itanu, mbere y'amatora rusange yo mu 2024.

Muri byo harimo ko Ubwongereza butazasubira mu isoko rusange ry'Uburayi (Single Market), mu ihuriro rya gasutamo (Customs Union), cyangwa ngo bwemere ubwisanzure busesuye bw'abaturage bwo kujya gutura no gukorera mu bihugu bigize uwo muryango.

Azavuga ko amahirwe yo kugirana amasezerano mashya ari inyungu ku mpande zombi kandi ko agaragaza "uburyo bushya bwo gukorana".

Ati: "Ntabwo ari uguhangana. Ntabwo ari ugukomeza gusenya ibiraro biduhuza. Ahubwo ni ugukorana mu buryo bwubaka kandi bwiza, tugaragaza ko dushobora guhuriza hamwe imbaraga mu guhangana n'ibibazo duhuriyeho."

Burnham yanze ko habaho impinduka zikomeye mu mubano w'Ubwongereza n'umuryango w'Ubumwe bw'Uburayi mbere y'amatora rusange ataha.

Icyakora, yagaragaje ko ashaka gusuzuma ibyiza n'ibibi by'uburyo butandukanye Ubwongereza bushobora gukoresha mu kugena umubano wabwo w'igihe kirekire n'uwo muryango.

Uwahoze ari minisitiri w'intebe, Sir Keir Starmer, yagiranye amasezerano n'uwo muryango muri Gicurasi(5) 2025, arebana n'uburobyi, ubucuruzi n'ibindi.

Inama yo muri iki cyumweru izaba umwanya kuri guverinoma y'Ubwongereza wo gushaka kumvikana ku zindi mpinduka.

Ubwongereza n'umuryango w'ubumwe bw'uburayi bamaze kumvikana ku mushinga w'amasezerano agamije gukuraho igenzura ryashyizweho nyuma ya Brexit ku biribwa n'ibikomoka ku buhinzi byoherezwa mu mahanga.

Imishinga y'andi masezerano ajyanye n'ubucuruzi bw'ibyuka bihumanya ikirere, ndetse na gahunda izaha urubyiruko amahirwe yo kujya mu bindi bihugu bigize uwo muryango gukora no gutembera, na yo yamaze kugezwa ku bihugu bigize EU.

Umuyobozi wungirije w'Ishyaka ry'aba "conservateurs", Alex Burghart, yavuze ko aho gukemura ikibazo cy'amafaranga agenda yiyongera akoreshwa mu mfashanyo z'imibereho, kuzahura ubukungu no gutera inkunga ibikenewe mu rwego rw'ingabo, Burnham arimo gutegura guha EU andi mafaranga kugira ngo arangaze abaturage ku bibazo ishyaka rye ryateje.

Ishyaka rya Liberal Democrats ryavuze mu ntangiriro z'uku kwezi ko umushinga w'amasezerano ku bicuruzwa by'ibiribwa ari "igisubizo cy'agateganyo, aho kuba igisubizo kirambye".

Ryavuze kandi ko igisubizo nyacyo ari uko Ubwongereza bwongera kwinjira ku isoko rusange ry'Uburayi kandi bukagirana ubumwe bwa gasutamo n'uwo muryango.

Ishyaka rya Reform UK ryavuze ko imwe mu nyungu z'ingenzi za Brexit ari uko Ubwongereza butagihatirwa "kubahiriza amategeko y'Uburayi adafite ishingiro", rinavuga ko uburyo ubwo ari bwo bwose bwo kongera guhuza amategeko y'Ubwongereza n'ay'uwo muryango bushobora kugira ingaruka mbi kuri politiki y'ubucuruzi bw'icyo gihugu.

Ishyaka rya Green Party ryo mu Bwongereza ryo ryasabye ko igihugu cyongera kwinjira mu ihuriro rya gasutamo ry'Uburayi. Umuyobozi waryo, Zack Polanski, yari aherutse kuvuga ko gusubira mu muryango w'Ubumwe bw'Uburayi mu buryo bwuzuye ari byo byaba igisubizo cyiza kurusha ibindi byose ku gihugu cy'Ubwongereza.

MN202611_1wfk65zc3kl.t:
You've done Liverpool and Scotland proud - Kenny Dalglish on Andy Robertson's career

Andy Robertson will become the most capped men's Scotland international if he earns his 103rd cap in Monday night's Nations League campaign closer in Switzerland.

Twelve years on from his debut - off the bench in a Poland friendly - he is set to surpass his friend and fellow Liverpool legend, Kenny Dalglish, whose record haul has stood for 40 years.

On moving level with the man they - and he - will always call King, the Tottenham Hotspur left-back shifted chat towards the former forward, his commendable humility laid bare.

But, in St Gallen, the spotlight will be brightly shone on one of Scotland's favourite sons as he goes solo at the summit.

Robertson set to make history, but hero Dalglish will always be King

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

Andy Robertson on his hero, Kenny Dalglish

For much of this year, Dalglish was the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' topped the list on 102 caps - earning his last in November 1996 against Luxembourg when in a player-manager role at Liverpool.

Few since have even come close to toppling him - even when Robertson does, he is keen to stress the throne is still reserved for Dalglish - but it is perhaps fitting it is the current captain, given their great friendship.

Which allows Dalglish to say he's not having any of it.

"He always says: 'You've got millions more games. Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

But not out of John McGinn's - the midfielder's double against North Macedonia on Friday having taken him to within six of the legendary duo.

The Aston Villa captain is lurking only eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time caps list, too, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 32 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now he is the only man to have led Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."

One of those young players is 20-year-old Findlay Curtis, who told the media the night before Robertson's potentially-historic night that his captain has "probably been the biggest role model" he's looked up to since joining the international set-up earlier this year.

Perhaps that was because Robertson did him a turn back in the day. Unbeknownst to the skipper.

Rangers winger Curtis was only 14 during the Covid pandemic and was partial to playing a bit of Fifa, and Robertson was a star in his team.

"I was just thinking, I had him in my Fifa team," he explained. "[For] defending and he was just fast as well.

"What a servant he has been for the country."

'I had him in my Fifa team!' - Findlay Curtis on going from fan to team-mate of Robertson

Robertson has played under four permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played five times for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair led Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 100 of his 102 caps, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with?

At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

Adam Abbou stars as Freddie in the hit BBC series This City Is Ours

With millions of viewers and a major role in a Bafta-nominated series, you might not expect Adam Abbou to know much about feeling self-conscious.

"When we were kids it wasn't so cool to be from Liverpool," the This City Is Ours actor says.

"I'd be in these rooms with people who were really posh and I always felt out of place."

The Liverpool-based BBC series has become a hit, with Abbou, who plays Freddie, stepping into a prominent role for its second season.

But it's not just the storylines on drugs, gangs and murders hooking audiences - it's the setting too, and the Scouse actors bringing it to life.

Created by Liverpudlian writer Stephen Butchard, This City Is Ours recruited heavily from Merseyside.

Lead actors James Nelson-Joyce, Jack McMullen and Mike Noble were all born in Liverpool, as was Abbou, who grew up in Anfield.

But like many young and aspiring actors, for a long time he thought where he came from could hold him back.

"I didn't see a lot of [Liverpudlian accents] on TV when I was a kid," the 23-year-old says.

As a result, acting "always felt really out of reach".

Abbou played the title role in a touring production of Billy Elliot the Musical in 2015, and has since appeared in dramas like Casualty, Time and Waterloo Road.

He says he wasn't expecting his latest gig, where he plays Freddie, gangster Banksey's son, to become so significant.

"If you would have asked me 10 years ago, I would have said you probably need to move to London," he says.

"So for me to be able to do a show like this in Liverpool, it just further proves that you can do it from anywhere."

The young actor says more needs to be done to improve working-class representation in TV

Abbou is passionate about promoting working-class stories and actors from underprivileged backgrounds, who he says are "some of the hardest working kids you'll ever come across".

While This City Is Ours provided him with his big break, he says more needs to be done across the industry to open doors.

New research from the Creative Industries Policy and Evidence Centre , external published last week found representation of people from working-class backgrounds has fallen over the past five years, from 25% in 2021 to 21% now.

"I think it's a trust issue," Abbou says, with producers less willing to take risks on new talent.

"But if you give a working-class kid a chance they will run with it and they won't let you down."

In January, the BBC committed to working harder to make sure people from different backgrounds were portrayed accurately and authentically in its output.

It followed a report that recommended the broadcaster could improve how it represented working-class communities, highlighting how their stories often focus on "themes of poverty, crime and addiction".

That's true for This City Is Ours, which follows the lives of drugs gangs, with Freddie becoming more involved in the business throughout the second series.

That portrayal of the city is something Liverpool's mayor said he wasn't happy about.

But Abbou insists he was confident about the series' ability to represent his hometown authentically and dismisses accusations it glamourises crime.

"I was never worried because Stephen [Butchard] roots all of his writing in Liverpool," he says.

"He is a Scouser, he knows what it's like to grow up a Scouser. The environment and gorgeous scenery of the city is always embedded in the script.

"It's a show that paints the city in a wonderful light. Of course the characters are flawed, but that's the nature of the show that we're creating."

Abbou was thrilled to be trusted with a more prominent role in the second series

From the reaction he's had locally, Abbou thinks the series has been a boost for Liverpool overall.

The reaction has been "quite crazy" in the city, he says, "but of course it would be because people love to see themselves and their accent reflected on TV and when it is, you almost feel like you know the person".

"It has truly been incredible to see the rise of the Scouse accent," he adds, crediting the Netflix series Adolescence, starring and co-created by Stephen Graham, with accelerating the change.

"Stephen Graham really was the one who started the wave for Scouse actors," he says.

"And then the likes of Jodie Comer and now you've got your Mike Nobles, your James Nelson-Joyces... and now your Adam Abbous.

"We're making waves for young Scouse talent."

As for what's next, Abbou says the series has helped push his career forward and he has some "exciting projects lined up" which he can't speak about just yet.

"I just want to do things that make me feel creatively fulfilled and mean something and have a voice."

Most of the second-round ties in the 2026-27 Women's FA Cup took place on Sunday

In years gone by, it was not unusual for FA Cup ties to require three attempts to complete as every drawn match would require another replay.

Nowadays, Women's FA Cup ties are decided on the day with extra time and penalties if needed.

Unless that tie is Lye Town v Peterborough United in the first round of the 2026-27 competition.

The match between the Women's National League sides has now been abandoned twice, and is yet to be completed.

The first go was abandoned because of a serious player injury, while the second on Sunday was called off amid bad weather.

It means that while most teams remaining in the competition are awaiting the third-round draw on Monday evening - when second-tier WSL2 sides enter the competition - Lye and Peterborough are still stuck in round one.

Fourth-tier Lye, of National League Division One Midlands, already had an unusual path to round one to face Peterborough of the National League Northern Premier, a division above.

Entering in the third qualifying round, their match against Coton Green was also postponed, so took place on October 22, after the first-round draw had been made.

A 5-0 win set up the Peterborough tie, due to be played on 8 November, a week after the other games.

It finally looked like the tie would be played to a conclusion as Lye led 1-0 with 12 minutes remaining.

But after a serious injury suffered by Lye goalkeeper Pharyn Ashton the match was abandoned and rescheduled again for 15 November.

This too proved in vain. Sunday's match was abandoned at half-time with Peterborough leading 3-1, because of a waterlogged pitch.

Spare a thought too for Rugby Borough, who are lined up to play the winner in round two but are also being forced to wait.

Collins picked up a knee injury in the closing stages against Austria on Saturday

Republic of Ireland captain Nathan Collins has been ruled out of Tuesday's must-win Nations League game against Kosovo with a knee injury.

Defender Collins picked up the issue in the closing stages of Saturday's 1-0 defeat by Austria in Linz and has returned to his club Brentford for treatment.

Queens Park Rangers' Jimmy Dunne will replace Collins - who also missed all four games of the September/October window - in the matchday squad for the Kosovo fixture.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has opted against drafting in Seamus Coleman, who is currently with the squad in a playing/coaching hybrid role.

"No, Jimmy Dunne will take Nathan's spot but we're really happy with what Seamus is giving to us," said Hallgrimsson.

"We obviously need to see the session today, that's the first session after the game, to see how players are but given everything I think we'll have the same squad including Jimmy."

Hallgrimsson rues 'painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland

The Republic of Ireland must win Tuesday's game to finish second in Group B3 and seal a place in March's promotion play-offs.

Hallgrimsson's side fell to a late 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in September before bouncing back to take four points from two matches against Israel.

"We need to get the same mentality, the same characters on the pitch against Kosovo," added Hallgrimsson.

"It is going to be as tough a game as it was in Austria, so just transfer that same attitude and if we do that, we will have a good byproduct, which is a win.

"It is clear we need to win the game, a draw will do nothing for us, and that is our mentality going into the game."

The Republic of Ireland's ultimate aim is securing a place at Euro 2028, which they will co-host alongside England, Wales and Scotland.

While goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher said playing in a tournament at home would be "amazing", he insisted the players are not looking that far ahead.

"Yeah, it would obviously be hard to describe, it would be an amazing experience, to play in a major tournament at home would be special," said the Brentford keeper.

"But I don't think we can think too far ahead into that. Obviously we've got to focus on tomorrow and trying to get a good result and we'll look towards that then when it comes.

"But we all know the opportunity that's there for us if we can perform, so it'll be a great opportunity."

Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season.

The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season.

He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real.

The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup.

"I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said.

"Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years.

"That may have affected my start to the season.

"On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season."

Vinicius received a red card for violent conduct in October when he pulled the hair of Villarreal midfielder Nathan Saliba, which led to a four-match suspension.

In his absence, record signing Yan Diomande has made the most of his opportunity on the left wing, scoring four goals.

Vinicius joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and has scored more than 20 club goals in each of his past five seasons.

Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, three points behind rivals Barcelona, and return to league action when they host Celta Vigo on Saturday.

PHNOM PENH – The contest over who should lead the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF) has exposed deep diplomatic divisions within an organization whose founding principle is to bring countries together through a shared language, cooperation and common values.

Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, whose second term as Secretary-General was due to end, has been granted a one-year extension after heads of state and government failed to reach an agreement on her successor during the summit in Phnom Penh.

The failure to resolve the leadership contest reflects a widening disagreement among member states over how the next Secretary-General should be selected. While one camp pushed for an election, others favored avoiding a vote in favor of reaching consensus on a single candidate.

The OIF recently amended its rules, making an election the preferred method of selecting the Secretary-General.

Under the new system, each member state has one vote, marking a departure from the previous practice, which prioritized consensus and gave considerable influence to major financial contributors such as Canada and France.

The stalemate followed days of intense diplomatic maneuvering, including an unsuccessful attempt by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye to persuade President Paul Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy.

According to diplomatic reporting by Africa Intelligence, a meeting convened at Faye’s initiative on the evening of November 15 failed to change Rwanda’s position, leaving member states unable to resolve the contest.

A Regional Dispute Enters the Francophonie

The strongest opposition to Mushikiwabo’s re-election came from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose government had put forward former Culture Minister Juliana Amato Lumumba as a candidate.

The Congolese government had also threatened to withdraw from the OIF should Mushikiwabo secure another term, raising the prospect of a major institutional setback for an organization already affected by the departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025.

In a last-minute change of strategy, the DRC announced its willingness to withdraw Lumumba’s candidacy and support Romania’s Dacian Cioloș, presenting the move as an attempt to find a consensus candidate and prevent the organization from becoming an extension of the Rwanda-DRC confrontation.

However, Rwanda questioned the logic of replacing an African candidate with a European one, particularly in light of an African Union decision adopted in July 2026 endorsing three African candidacies and calling on African OIF members to rally behind one of them.

“The DRC’s announced support for the Romanian candidate Dacian Cioloș, at the expense of the two other African women candidates, is a flagrant violation,” Nduhungirehe said in a statement.

France’s Influence and the Question of Consensus

France, which has considerable influence within the Francophone world as one of the organization’s largest financial contributors, found itself at the center of the diplomatic contest.

Canada, together with its associated provinces, contributes €19.4 million to the OIF, while France contributes €19.3 million.

Their financial contributions have traditionally given them considerable weight in the organization’s affairs, adding another dimension to the debate over how its leadership should be decided.

President Emmanuel Macron reportedly sought to persuade Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy, with Paris presenting its intervention as an effort to preserve the organization’s unity.

Rwanda, however, viewed the pressure as interference in a decision that should be left to member states.

The disagreement has revived questions about the extent to which former colonial powers should influence leadership decisions in an organization that brings together countries from Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.

The irony is particularly striking given Mushikiwabo’s own warning during the summit’s opening proceedings against allowing bilateral disputes to undermine the organization.

“The OIF is not a defensive alliance, and its unity does not require uniformity of positions. Members should resist turning the organization into a platform for bilateral disputes,” she said.

Its value, she added, lies in the ability of members to meet on an equal footing and turn their diversity into a source of influence and trust.

Macron similarly appealed for unity, warning against internal fractures and arguing that the organization’s strength depended on preserving cohesion among its members.

A Leadership Decision with Wider Consequences

Beyond the contest over one position, the failure to agree on the next Secretary-General raises questions about the future direction and credibility of the OIF.

The organization brings together 90 states and governments, including 53 full members, making it a significant platform for political dialogue, cultural cooperation and international engagement.

Its membership stretches well beyond countries where French is the dominant language, reflecting a broader ambition to build partnerships across continents.

The departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025 had already demonstrated how political disagreements can weaken that ambition. Losing the DRC, one of the largest French-speaking countries in the world, would further undermine the organization’s continental reach and influence.

For Mushikiwabo, the one-year extension offers continuity after eight years at the helm, but it also leaves the question of her longer-term future unresolved.

The failure to settle the leadership contest has exposed the difficulty of reconciling competing national interests under a system that is increasingly expected to rely on voting rather than consensus.

The question facing the OIF is therefore whether an organization built around linguistic and cultural ties can remain a credible multilateral platform when political rivalries among its members threaten to overshadow the common interests that brought them together.

Perezida wa Repubulika y’u Rwanda, Paul Kagame, yitabiriye umunsi wa nyuma w’Inama ya 20 y’Umuryango w’Ibihugu bikoresha ururimi rw'Igifaransa (OIF), yabereye i Phnom Penh muri Cambodia, aho abayobozi baganiriye ku gushimangira amahoro no kuyubaka nk’inshingano ihuriweho n’ibihugu bigize uyu muryango.

Muri iyi nama yabaye kuri uyu wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026, Perezida Kagame yifatanyije n’abandi bakuru b’ibihugu na za Guverinoma mu biganiro byibanze ku buryo ibihugu bigize OIF byafatanya mu gushimangira amahoro, kurinda umutekano no kwimakaza ubufatanye.

Ibiganiro byagarutse ku mahoro nk’inshingano isaba uruhare rwa buri gihugu, aho ibihugu bigomba gushyira imbere ubufatanye n’ibisubizo bihuriweho mu gukumira amakimbirane no guharanira umutekano urambye.

Ibiganiro byagarutse ku mahoro nk’inshingano isaba uruhare rwa buri gihugu, aho ibihugu bigomba gushyira imbere ubufatanye n’ibisubizo bihuriweho mu gukumira amakimbirane no guharanira umutekano urambye.

Iyi nama yasojwe hafashwe icyemezo cyo kongerera Louise Mushikiwabo manda y’umwaka umwe yo gukomeza kuyobora Umuryango Mpuzamahanga w’Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF), mu gihe cy’inzibacyuho.

Iki cyemezo kigamije gutuma ubuyobozi bw’uyu muryango bukomeza nta gihungabanye, mu gihe OIF yongera kwibanda ku nshingano zayo z’ingenzi no gushaka umwuka w’ubufatanye hagati y’ibihugu biyigize.

Icyo gihe cy’inzibacyuho kandi kigamije gufasha mu kurangiza ukutumvikana n’impaka zidatanga umusaruro, by’umwihariko izishingiye ku kutumvikana kudafite umurongo uhamye, kugira ngo umuryango wongere gushyira imbaraga mu byo washyiriweho.

Louise Mushikiwabo amaze imyaka 7 ayobora OIF kuko yahiye muri izo nshingano bwa mbere mu 2019, nyuma yo gutorerwa kuyobora uyu muryango mu nama yabereye i Yerevan muri Armenia. Yongeye gutorerwa manda ya kabiri mu 2022, yari iteganyijwe kurangira mu 2026.

Inama ya 20 ya OIF yabereye i Phnom Penh muri Cambodia, yari ihurije hamwe abakuru b’ibihugu na za Guverinoma, abayobozi b’imiryango mpuzamahanga n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa, baganira ku bibazo bireba ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa n’uburyo byafatanya mu kubishakira ibisubizo.

Iyi gahunda yatangiye kuri uyu wa Mbere, tariki ya 16 Ugushyingo 2026, ikaba ishyirwa mu bikorwa n’Ikigo cy’Igihugu cy’Ubuzima (RBC), aho abujuje ibisabwa bazajya bahabwa uru rukingo ku Bigo Nderabuzima byo mu gihugu hose kandi nta kiguzi.

Abazakingirwa bazahabwa doze ebyiri, aho iya kabiri izatangwa nyuma y’amezi atandatu umuntu ahawe iya mbere.

RBC ivuga ko umuntu uzajya kwikingiza azasabwa kwerekana indangamuntu cyangwa ikindi cyangombwa cyemewe kigaragaza imyaka ye, kugira ngo hagenzurwe niba yujuje ibisabwa.

Ibi bije bisanga gahunda yari isanzweho yo gukingira abangavu bafite imyaka 12, ndetse n’izindi serivisi zo gusuzuma no kuvura kanseri y’inkondo y’umura.

Kanseri y’inkondo y’umura ni imwe mu ndwara zishobora kwirindwa binyuze mu gukingira no gusuzuma hakiri kare. Icyakora, RBC igaragaza ko igikomeje kuba ikibazo gikomeye ku buzima bw’abagore mu Rwanda, aho igize hafi 13% by’abarwayi ba kanseri bose.

U Rwanda ruvuga ko kongera umubare w’abakingirwa biri mu ngamba rushyira imbere mu kwihutisha intego yo kurandura iyi ndwara bitarenze mu 2027.

Iyi gahunda kandi ihuye n’intego z’Ishami ry’Umuryango w’Abibumbye ryita ku Buzima (OMS) zo kurandura kanseri y’inkondo y’umura ku isi bitarenze mu 2030, binyuze ku ntego zizwi nka 90-70-90.

Izi ntego ziteganya ko nibura 90% by’abangavu baba barakingiwe kanseri y’inkondo y’umura mbere yo kuzuza imyaka 15; 70% by’abagore baba barasuzumwe kanseri y’inkondo y’umura bafite imyaka 35 na 45; naho 90% by’abagore basanzwemo iyi kanseri cyangwa ibimenyetso byayo bakabona ubuvuzi bukwiye.

U Rwanda rwihaye intego yo kurandura kanseri y’inkondo y’umura bitarenze mu 2027, kandi kwagura gahunda yo gukingira ikagera ku bagore n’abakobwa bafite imyaka 30–45 ni imwe mu ngamba zitezweho kugira uruhare mu kuyigeraho.

Amatora yo guhitamo Umunyamabanga Mukuru mushya w’Umuryango Mpuzamahanga w’Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF) yasubitsweho umwaka wose, nyuma y’uko ibihugu biwugize binaniwe kumvikana ku muntu uzayobora uyu muryango mu gihe cy’imyaka ine iri imbere.

Iki cyemezo cyafatiwe i Phnom Penh muri Cambodia ku wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026, nyuma y'ibiganiro byamaze amasaha menshi hagati y'abakuru b'ibihugu na za Guverinoma bitabiriye inama ya 20 ya Francophonie.

Louise Mushikiwabo, Umunyarwandakazi wari umaze imyaka umunani ayobora uyu muryango, azakomeza inshingano ze kugeza mu Ugushyingo 2027, ariko mu bwumvikane bwagezweho hagati y'ibihugu binyamuryango, u Rwanda ntiruzatanga umukandida mu matora azakurikiraho.

Isubikwa ry'aya matora ni ubwa mbere ribaye kuva umwanya w'Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa Francophonie washyirwaho mu 1997. Ibi bigaragaza ubukana bw'impaka za dipolomasi zari zimaze iminsi hagati y'ibihugu byari bishyigikiye abakandida batandukanye, cyane cyane u Rwanda na Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC).

Impamvu amatora yahindutse ikibazo cya Dipolomasi

Mu ntangiriro, aya matora y'Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF yari ateganyijwe kuri uyu wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026, hagamijwe guhitamo ugomba gusimbura Louise Mushikiwabo cyangwa akaguma muri izo nshingano cyane ko nawe yari umukandida wongeye gutangwa n'u Rwanda muri Manda ya gatatu.

Mushikiwabo yatangiye kuyobora OIF mu 2018, asimbuye Umunya-Canada Michaëlle Jean, maze yongera gutorerwa indi manda mu 2022.

Ariko kandidatire ye kuri Manda ya gatatu yaje kurwanywa bikomeye na RDC, igihugu kimaze igihe gifitanye umwuka mubi n'u Rwanda nyuma y'ibirego gihora gishyira imbere by'uko rugira uruhare mu bibazo by'umutekano mu burasirazuba bwa Congo.

Ubutegetsi bwa Perezida Tshisekedi, bumaze igihe ku rwego mpuzamahanga bwaragize iturufu ibibazo byo mu burasirazuba aho rushinja u Rwanda gushyigikira umutwe wa M23 ukorera mu burasirazuba bwa RDC ndetse rukanasaba ibihugu n'imiryango kurukomatanyiriza. Ni ibirego nyamara u Rwanda rutahwemye guhakana no kugaragaza impamvu muzi yabyo n'uburyo bikwiye gukemurwa.

Iyi ntambara ya dipolomasi Repubulika Iharanira Demukarasi ya Congo yaje no kuyinjiza mu matora ya OIF, aho iki Gihugu cyagaragaje ko kitazigera gishyigikira ko Mushikiwabo ahabwa indi manda, ndetse inavuga ko izahita yivana mu banyamuryango ba OIF mu gihe yakongera gutorwa.

Ibi bivuze ko aya amatora atari akiri ikibazo cyo guhitamo umuntu ufite ubushobozi bwo kuyobora OIF nk'uko Louise Mushikiwabo yakomeje kubivuga mu bihe bitandukanye ko umuntu ugomba kuyobora atagomba kureberwa mu ndorerwamo y'ibibazo bya politike ahubwo akwiye kureberwa mu bushobozi bwe nicyo azamarira uyu muryango.

Ni amatora bigaragara ko yari yamaze guhinduka ikibazo cy'imibanire hagati y'ibihugu bibiri byo mu Karere k'Ibiyaga Bigari.

Abakandida bane n'ibihugu byari bibashyigikiye

Urugendo rwo kwiyamamaza ku mwanya w'Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF, hari abakandida bane bari bari bahataniye uyu mwanya. Harimo Louise Mushikiwabo w'u Rwanda, Juliana Amato Lumumba wa RDC, Dacian Cioloș wahoze ari Minisitiri w'Intebe wa Romania, na Coumba Bâ wo muri Mauritania.

Mu gihe imyiteguro y'amatora yari igeze kure, RDC yatangaje ko ikuyeho kandidatire ya Juliana Amato Lumumba, igashyigikira Dacian Cioloș, mu rwego rwo gushaka umukandida umwe ugomba kumvikanwaho n'ibihugu byinshi.

Iyo ukurikiranyye neza byo RDC yari ikoze, bivuze ko icyemezo yari ifashe cyari kigamije guhuza imbaraga n'ibihugu bitari bishyigikiye manda ya gatatu ya Mushikiwabo. Ku rundi ruhande, u Rwanda rwakomeje gushyigikira Mushikiwabo ndetse rugaragaza ko nta mpamvu yatuma rukuraho kandidatire ye.

Jeune Afrique mu cyumweru gishize yari yatangaje ko Perezida w’u Bufaransa, Emmanuel Macron, yasabye mugenzi we w'u Rwanda Paul Kagame gukuramo kandidatire ya Louise Mushikiwabo kugira ngo RDC itivana muri uyu muryango.

Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga, Olivier Nduhungirehe, mu kiganiro yagiranye n'itangazamakuru yavuze ko Mushikiwabo Louise akiri umukandida w’u Rwanda mu matora y’Umunyamabanga Mukuru wa OIF, kandi ko u Rwanda atari Igihugu gihabwa amategeko avuye ku kindi Gihugu.

KUKI BATAKORESHEJE AMATORA NGO HAMENYEKANE UTSINZE?

Amategeko ya OIF ashyira imbere guhitamo Umunyamabanga Mukuru binyuze mu bwumvikane bw'ibihugu biyigize. Iyo ubwumvikane butabonetse, hashobora gukoreshwa amatora y'ibanga, aho umukandida atsinda binyuze mu majwi menshi.

Gusa kuri iyi nshuro, hari ibihugu byashakaga ko amatora akorwa kugira ngo ikibazo gikemurwe hakurikijwe amajwi. Ariko nyamara ibindi bigashimangira ko hakenewe kubanza kuboneka umukandida wumvikanwaho, kugira ngo amatora atavamo amakimbirane n'amacakubiri akomeye.

By'umwihariko, u Bufaransa na Canada, nk'ibihugu biri by'ingenzi bitera inkunga OIF kandi bikagira ijambo rikomeye byashishikarizaga ibihugu gushaka ubwumvikane no kurinda ubumwe bw'uyu muryango.

Mu gihe ibiganiro byakomeje kutagera ku mwanzuro, ibihugu byahisemo gusubika amatora umwaka wose, aho guhatira impande zitavuga rumwe kujya mu matora ashobora gukurura umwuka mubi.

Ni icyemezo cyafashwe mu rwego rwo guha ibihugu umwanya wo kongera kuganira, ndetse no gutegura impinduka mu buryo uyu muryango uzajya uhitamo umuyobozi wawo.

RDC YIKANZE INTSINZI YIKOMANGA KU GATUZA

Kuri RDC, isubikwa ry'amatora rifatwa nk'intsinzi ya dipolomasi, kuko ryatumye icyifuzo cyayo cyo kutongera gutorwa kwa Louise Mushikiwabo muri manda ya gatatu kigera ku ntego zayo.

Ibi byatumye Minisitiri w'Ububanyi n'Amahanga wa RDC, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, ajya ku rubuga rwe rwa X, agaragaza ko igihugu cye gishyigikiye ubwumvikane bwagezweho, maze abwita ko ari igisubizo cyiza kigamije kurinda ubumwe bw'ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa.

Ikindi RDC yungutse muri iri subikwa ry'aya matora ni uko kandidatire ya Juliana Amato Lumumba itazahita ivaho burundu, kuko abakandida bari basanzwe bari mu ihatana bazongera guhabwa amahirwe yo kwiyamamaza mu gihe amatora azaba yongeye gutegurwa nubwo ibi bitavuze ko ariwe mukandida ukwiye koko ugomba kuyobora umuryango wa OIF.

Nyuma y'uyu mwanzuro wo gusubika amatora kandi RDC yirinze gufata icyemezo cyo kuva muri OIF, ikintu cyari kugira ingaruka zikomeye kuri uyu muryango cyane ko nicyo gihugu gifite abaturage benshi bavuga Igifaransa muri uyu Muryango Mpuzamahanga w'Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa.

Ibi biri mu byo RDC yagize iturufu ikomeye kuko byatumye ibindi bihugu bigaragaza ko kuba yaba muri OIF byari kuba igihombo gikomeye ku muryango ushingiye ku guteza imbere ururimi rw'Igifaransa n'ubufatanye hagati y'ibihugu birukoresha.

Gusa gusubika aya matora ndetse nibikangisho bya Repubulika Iharanira Demukarasi ya Congo, ntibisobanuye ko yamaze kubona umwanya w'Umunyamabanga Mukuru.

KUKI GUKANGISHA KUVA MURI OIF KWA RDC MURI OIF BYARI IKIBAZO GIKOMEYE?

OIF ihuza ibihugu n'imiryango 90, birimo ibifite ubunyamuryango busesuye 53, ibifite ubunyamuryango budasesuye bitanu n'ibifite umwanya w'indorerezi 32.

Repubulika Iharanira Demukarasi ya Congo ni kimwe mu bihugu bifite umubare munini w'abavuga Igifaransa ku Isi babarirwa kuri miliyoni 100, bityo kuba yari yatangaje ko ishobora kuva muri uyu muryango Louise Mushikiwabo aramutse yongeye gutorerwa kuyobora OIF, byari impungenge zikomeye ku bihugu bigize uyu muryango.

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a string of online crimes, including trying to extort the makers of Grand Theft Auto 6 after stealing dozens of unfinished clips of the game.

21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, carried out the hack in 2022, and was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

On Monday, Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj breached Rockstar Games in 2022 whilst he was on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.

He was being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to protect him from rival hackers who threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

GTA 6 will feature brand new protagonists Jason and Lucia - the first playable female character in any of the 3D games

The company refused to cooperate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.79m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

At the time, doctors deemed Kurtaj unfit to stand in a traditional trial due to the severity of his autism, so instead he was given what is known as a trial of the facts.

The jury was asked to determine whether or not he committed the alleged acts - not if he did so with criminal intent.

In December 2023 the court ruled that he would remain at a secure hospital for life unless doctors deem him no longer a danger.

A routine assessment late last year deemed that he was now fit to stand a criminal trial which was scheduled to take place at Woolwhich Crown Court.

But Kurtaj pleaded guilty to all offences.

He sat in the dock with short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt but no tie.

The now 21-year-old blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his name, and pled guilty to all counts with no visible emotion.

The proscution described Kurtaj as a 'leading light' in the teen gang Lapsus$

Those included hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

The court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers whilst in custody including multiple biting incidents.

Whilst in prison he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

Kurtaj will be sentenced at a later date.

Kurtaj's Snapchat posts were the first sign for reporters that he had been released from a secure hospital

In the 2023 original trial, another Lapsus$ member, who was 17, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court.

The 17-year-old, who could not be named at the time due to his age, was sentenced to an 18-month Youth Rehabilitation Order, including intense supervision and a ban on using VPNs online.

Earlier this year that same hacker, now named as Thalha Jubair, was jailed for five years and six months after continuing his cyber crime offences with another group known as Scattered Spider.

Amongst victims was Transport for London which was subjected to a disruptive cyber attack that caused around £39m of damage and caused chaos inside the firm.

When a bartender asked James Bond in 2006's Casino Royale whether he'd like his vodka martini shaken or stirred, the irritated spy replied: "Do I look like I give a damn?"

Such throwaway lines were a clever way of signalling to the audience that this was a new era for 007 - and that the film series launched in 1962 was being overhauled with the arrival of Daniel Craig.

Over the next few films, producers struck a balance between nodding to the past while also moving away from some of the cheesier elements of the series, no longer sticking rigidly to all of the tradition and tropes of Bond.

"Were you expecting an exploding pen?" Ben Whishaw's Q later asked the secret service agent in Skyfall. "We don't really go in for that anymore."

Two decades on from Craig's debut, the series is about to be rebooted once again, with a new actor and new creative team. It's an exciting time for Bond fans as they wait to see what shape the next era will take. Here's what we know so far.

Pattinson is known for films including Twilight, The Batman and Tenet

British actor Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next actor to play James Bond.

He shot to fame as Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, and went on to star in Twilight.

Pattinson appeared opposite Kristen Stewart in the series of five films based on Stephenie Meyers' vampire novels.

He has gone on to star in other major films and franchises including The Batman and Christopher Nolan's recent adaptation of The Odyssey.

But Pattinson is also respected within the industry for his unusual choice of roles, often appearing in independent, arthouse and experimental films.

His other credits include The Lighthouse, Mickey 17, Life, The Drama, Good Time, Primetime, The Rover, Bel Ami, Tenet and The Lost City of Z.

L-R: Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Jack Barton are all thought to have auditioned for the role

A handful of actors were thought to have made it to the final screen tests before Pattinson scored Britain's biggest film role. They included:

Jack Lowden , 36 - whose credits include Slow Horses and Pride and Prejudice

Josh O'Connor , 36 - The Crown, Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery

Callum Turner , 36 - Masters of the Air, The Capture

Jack Barton , 31 - Heartstopper, SAS: Rogue Heroes

Nicholas Hoult , 36 - About A Boy, Superman

Paul Mescal , 30 - Normal People, Gladiator II

But while many of the names are seen as hot, up-and-coming actors, Pattinson was arguably the most bankable movie star.

The film is expected to go into production in 2027, before its release in 2028. No exact dates have been announced.

Film schedules can be notoriously fluid, but it's clear that development is well under way, with the director and writer already in place.

It will be the 26th film in the official film series, but the title has not yet been confirmed.

Steven Knight (left) will write the script, while Denis Villeneuve will direct the film

The movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve , known for Prisoners, Sicario, Arrival, Blade Runner 2049 and the recent Dune trilogy starring Timothée Chalamet.

"Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007," the French-Canadian director said last year. "I grew up watching James Bond films with my father, ever since Dr. No with Sean Connery. I'm a die-hard Bond fan. To me, he's sacred territory."

He added: "I intend to honour the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come. This is a massive responsibility, but also, incredibly exciting for me and a huge honour."

Bond 26 will be written by Steven Knight , known for TV series such as Peaky Blinders and House of Guinness, and films including Burnt, Spencer, Locke and The Girl in the Spider's Web.

Knight has said it had always been on his "bucket list" to write a Bond film, adding that he felt he was "doing my duty for King and country" by joining the franchise.

He told the BBC he planned to "write the character, not the actor", adding: "The thing with Bond is it's its own universe and franchise. So there are certain rules.

"Obviously you have to move it along, but I love where it sits. I love that it's British. I love that it's not DC or Marvel... So I feel a responsibility to the text."

Irish actor Pierce Brosnan starred in four Bond films, including 1999's The World Is Not Enough

Sean Connery starred in six official Bond films between 1962 and 1971

George Lazenby starred in just one Bond film, in 1969

Roger Moore starred in seven Bond films between 1973 and 1985

Timothy Dalton starred in two Bond films, in 1987 and 1989

Pierce Brosnan starred in four Bond films, between 1995 and 2002

Daniel Craig starred in five Bond films between 2006 and 2021

You might have noticed some overlap in the above dates.

That's because Connery returned to the lead role for 1971's Diamonds Are Forever, after Lazenby took his place for 1969's On Her Majesty's Secret Service.

Connery also later appeared in 1983's Never Say Never Again, a Bond film produced by a different studio and not part of the official film series.

Roger Moore pictured filming 1985's A View To A Kill

If you discount the films not in the official series, there have been 25 Bond films in total. In order, they are:

Daniel Craig (pictured with co-star Léa Seydoux) stepped down as Bond with 2021's No Time To Die

With the change in ownership and a new creative team now in place, the new Bond film is likely to make a fresh start.

It would be difficult to continue the story chronologically given the ending of 2021's No Time To Die, but that still leaves producers with plenty of options.

A different version of James Bond, who exists in a different universe, would be easily pulled off in an era where audiences are used to major film franchises restarting in a different world or timeline.

Bond 26 could even be set in a significantly earlier era - an idea that gained more popularity after Tony Gilroy revealed he and fellow director Steven Soderbergh previously pitched a 1960s version , external of Bond.

Separately, actor Ralph Fiennes recently said , external he had once been in talks to play Bond, and had suggested producers make a "black and white and very sort of film noir-y" version set in the 1950s.

Neither idea materialised, but the suggestion went down well with some Bond fans, who noted a period piece would help make the film truer to Ian Fleming's original character and books.

Exactly what shape the next film takes will become clear at a later stage. For now, Christmas has come early for fans who have been waiting for years to find out who the next 007 will be.

Crystal Palace will be Thomas Frank's third London club after previous spells with Brentford and Tottenham

"When the time is right I will look forward to my return as a manager, ready to embrace the job with great energy and dedication," said Thomas Frank in June.

That time is now as the Dane is set to be announced as the new boss of Crystal Palace , who are two points and a goal difference deficit away from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.

Former Palace head coach Pierre Sage was sacked last week after just 16 league and cup games.

The role offers Frank an opportunity to rebuild his reputation after he was sacked by Tottenham in February after eight months.

But how big a challenge is the man who made his name at Brentford facing at Selhurst Park?

"It's going to be a bit of a shock for Thomas Frank," former West Ham and England goalkeeper Rob Green tells BBC Sport.

"He had his success at Brentford - a very well-run club where players are brought in with a lot of thinking and planning to take over the players they sell for profit.

"That doesn't happen at Crystal Palace .

"They lose players and then have a mad scramble to get players in. They have a team that has been decimated by sales and not replaced by the same quality.

"Thomas Frank needs to find something within that team that builds and garners the belief that means that they can compete in the Premier League, because it feels a long way short of that right now."

Will Frank prove the right fit for Palace and haul the Eagles out of the relegation zone?

Since getting the sack at Tottenham after 26 league games last season, Frank has been out of management longer than he was in charge of Spurs .

In the summer he released a statement in which he said "there have been conversations and opportunities" to return to management, but that he had "decided not to rush into the next role".

Frank's name was heavily linked with Palace before they went for a head coach with no Premier League experience to replace Oliver Glasner - the man who delivered an FA Cup, a Conference League title and Community Shield before moving to Nottingham Forest .

"Palace had one of the best managers they have had, if not forever, silverware coming across the doorstep. Look at what they achieved last season and instead of building on that, they dismantled a team," said former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.

Frank once described managing as being on a "hamster wheel" and a "crazy circus". , external

So why does he feel now is the right moment to return to management at a club propping up the table?

Frank, who was part of BBC Sport's World Cup punditry team during the summer, will be coming into the job refreshed and with renewed energy and enthusiasm following several months out of the game.

Between his appointment as Brentford boss in October 2018 and the sack at Tottenham earlier this year, he managed without a break for seven years and four months.

Spending the past few months away from Premier League pressure has allowed Frank, in his own words, to "study, observe and learn from other leaders both within sport and beyond".

Will his positivity and passion rub off on a Palace team who have lost seven times in 10 top-flight matches?

Would Thomas Frank be a good fit for Crystal Palace?

Frank, who places a major emphasis on set-piece organisation, will have to hit the ground running at Palace, who have lost their past four league games.

They have conceded more goals than anyone else in the Premier League (24) and have scored only 10 themselves.

"If you want someone to go in and restore some stability and defensive solidity while improving the set-piece element of the team, then Thomas Frank is the perfect man for the job," Times football writer Tom Allnutt told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.

With the Premier League season just 10 games old, Frank certainly has time to turn it around and will have targets in mind when the transfer window opens in January.

Palace sold France centre-back Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for £52m and Colombia right-back Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest for £22m during the summer transfer window.

Allnutt added: "We know they have sold so many good players and so far I don't think they have really replaced them adequately."

Another challenge for Frank is getting midfielder Adam Wharton, who has not played for England since March, back to something like his best form.

These are all challenges the new manager will relish.

After his bruising experience at Tottenham - having established Brentford in the Premier League - Frank has decided to climb back on the hamster wheel with Palace.

" Crystal Palace and Thomas Frank feels like a very good fit," added Robinson.

Thomas Frank has a lot of work to do as Crystal Palace have undoubtedly been the worst team in the Premier League so far this season, ranking bottom not just in points (seven) but also goal difference (-14) and expected goal difference (-8.1).

It's the defence where Frank will have to focus most of his attention. Not only have Palace conceded the most goals (24) but they've also faced the most shots (189) and have the worst expected goals against (xGA) figure in the league (21.9).

Their attack has actually not been too bad. While only Hull have taken fewer shots, the Eagles have created really good chances and have perhaps been unlucky not to score a few more goals given the opportunities they've had.

There is also one significant factor in Frank's favour. Although Palace may be bottom of the Premier League, they are certainly not cut adrift as they sit just two points from safety.

The side propping up the table at this stage have had an average of just three points in the past 10 seasons, but for as bad as they've been, Palace have seven - the most the bottom side have had after 10 games for 24 years.

MN202611_1vtzv5ksrme.t:
Robert Pattinson has starred in films including the Twilight franchise and The Batman

Robert Pattinson's career is already flying high with roles in films including the Twilight series, The Batman and The Odyssey, so signing up to play James Bond will propel his profile into the stratosphere.

He's already established himself as a leading man, action star and character actor, which is clearly why he is about to play the suave, British secret agent 007.

At 40, he is slightly older than some of the other men reportedly lined up for the role, but he's also the most famous - something the new Bond studio Amazon-MGM may have favoured, with an eye on the box office.

His recent work has garnered both critical and box office success, including Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster The Odyssey, in which he played the villainous Antinous.

Pattinson was also called "Oscar-worthy" by the Independent and "superb" by The Times, for his performance in November's Primetime, as the real-life host of US TV show To Catch a Predator.

He also helped lead 2022's The Batman to the second-biggest North American opening of the Covid-19 pandemic behind Spider-Man: No Way Home. The Guardian said he played the "brooding" role with " appealing vulnerability , external ".

Meanwhile in dark romantic comedy The Drama - one of three films he appeared in with Zendaya this year - he and his co-star gave a "career-highlight performance" , external .

Robert Pattinson starred in 2022's The Batman, which was described by critics as a grim, gritty, and gripping super-noir

Born in Barnes, south-west London, Pattinson grew up with his father, a classic car trader and mother, who worked at a modelling agency, and two elder sisters.

His interest in acting started while he was still at school, when he joined the Barnes Theatre Club.

"I wouldn't be acting if it wasn't for that little club," he told Your Local Guardian in 2008 , external .

"I went originally because a lot of pretty girls went there," he said. "I worked backstage and I started acting when all the good people left and I was the only one tall enough to play the lead.

"In a weird sort of way, that stuff was probably the best I've done and the stuff I am most proud of."

He landed his first big film role more than two decades ago, playing Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. A relatively minor character, but it was enough to get him noticed.

Three years later, he had a starring role in the first of five Twilight films, along with Kristen Stewart, in which they played star-crossed lovers - vampire Edward Cullen and mortal-turned vampire Kristen Stewart.

Based on Stephanie Meyer's hugely popular young adult books, the films globally grossed more than $3bn (£2.2bn) by 2012, and established Pattinson as a heartthrob.

He spoke in his early career of finding his often adoring, screaming fans hard to deal with.

"Although is part of the job, it feels like they have been paid to turn up and scream at me at 7.30pm," he said.

"Nothing I don't think can prepare you for the fans. I don't know why I'm not getting used to it but I'm completely overwhelmed every time."

Robert Pattinson and Kristen Stewart starred in five Twilight films from 2005 to 2012

In 2010, Time included him in their list of 100 people who "most affect our world" , external , saying perhaps prophetically that "we haven't seen a tenth of what he can do on screen".

After such mainstream success with the Twilight franchise, Pattinson was able to branch out.

He went on to work with several acclaimed independent film directors including David Cronenberg, starring in his film Cosmpopolis in 2012, as well as working with Werner Herzog in 2015's Queen of the Desert and The Lighthouse (2019), directed by Robert Eggers.

Pattinson told Screen Daily why he took the role in psychological horror film The Lighthouse , external , saying he told Eggers: "I just want to do something weird."

Pattinson and Zendaya have appeared in three films together this year - The Drama, The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three

The following year though, he was back in big-studio territory, with Odyssey director Christopher Nolan, in sci-fi thriller Tenet, and again in 2022 with The Batman, directed by Matt Reeves and co-starring Zoe Kravitz and Paul Dano.

Pattinson told Screen Daily why he returned to big-budget films, explaining: "I guess I was trying to do the opposite of what I've been doing. I started thinking, 'I really want to do a big thing.'

"I hadn't done something with a massive budget for ages. But you approach it exactly the same way."

The Batman got generally positive reviews, re-establishing Pattinson with a broader range of fans.

By 2025, when he was on the red carpet for Parasite director Bong Joon Ho's sci-fi black comedy, Mickey 17, he said it was "quite strange" to have a fanbase that was now dominated by men , external .

"There's like a bunch of guys, which is a new one for me!" he told the Associated Press.

Pattinson's private life has often created interest in the press, not least his previous relationships with Stewart, and then the singer FKA Twigs.

Since 2018, he has been in a relationship with model Suki Waterhouse. They got engaged in December 2023 and had their first child, a daughter, in March.

Robert Pattinson and Suki Waterhouse have been a couple since 2018

With his latest role as James Bond, Pattinson will be extremely busy, not least because the forthcoming Batman sequel is reportedly due out in 2028.

But the actor will have a head start as 007, having already worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve, who also helmed Dune: Part Three.

Pattinson was full of praise for him on their most recent film, despite the strain of working in the furnace-like heat of the desert.

"The scale of this stuff is just unbelievable, you're having your own Dune theme park, where the gimbal is going upside down and flying, and this is not like work at all," he told the New York Times , external .

"There are no negatives. Apart from having your sweat drained out of the top of your head, and getting like bulbous sweat bubbles. But even then, I didn't even really notice them.

"He's so easy to work with, Denis, it's never really a stress."

Sounds like Pattinson will have the cool head needed to juggle his forthcoming roles - including James Bond. You could even say he may end up being shaken, but not stirred.

The Kerch bridge was built in 2018 and is one of President Putin's signature infrastructure projects (file photo)

Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.

The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.

Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.

The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war.

The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.

The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.

Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment.

Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation.

Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children.

Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country.

Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect.

Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member.

The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia.

The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement.

A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US.

But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input.

"We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov.

EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".

British singer Raye leads the charge at this year's Grammy Awards with 11 nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumous nods.

Raye is nominated for her latest Mercury-winning record This Album May Contain Hope and its lead single Where Is My Husband!, which is up for both song and record of the year.

Parton's two nominations, both in the best country duo/group performance category, come three months after the country music star died aged 80.

Parton is recognised for Butterfly, her collaboration with the Zac Brown Band, and Light of a Clear Blue Morning, alongside an all-star line-up including her goddaughter Miley Cyrus.

Kongererwa umwaka umwe ku buyobozi bw’Umuryango w’Ibihugu bikoresha Igifaransa (OIF) kuri Louise Mushikiwabo bisobanuye ko azakomeza kuyobora uwo muryango kugeza mu Ugushyingo 2027, aho kuva kuri uwo mwanya binyuze mu matora.

Kwemezwa k'umwaka umwe ku ugomba kuyobora uyu muryango, ni igihe cy’inzibacyuho cyemejwe n’abakuru b’ibihugu na za Guverinoma zigize OIF, ubwo bahuriraga mu nama ya 20 i Phnom Penh muri Cambodia, ku wa 16 Ugushyingo 2026.

Impamvu nyamukuru ni uko ibihugu bigize OIF byananiwe kumvikana ku muntu wagombaga kuyobora indi manda y’imyaka ine, mu bakandida bane bahataniraga uwo mwanya, barimo Umunyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo, Umunyaromaniya Dacian Cioloș, Umunyamuritaniya Coumba Bâ n’Umunyekongo Juliana Lumumba.

Ibihugu 53 bifite uburenganzira bwo gutora, byahisemo gusubika amatora y’umuyobozi mushya kugira ngo habanze hashakwe umukandida ushobora kumvikanwaho na benshi.

Nubwo Mushikiwabo azakomeza kuyobora OIF mu gihe cy’umwaka umwe wongeweho, ariko U Rwanda rwiyemeje kutazongera gutanga umukandida kuri uwo mwanya nyuma y’icyo gihe.

Umwaka agiye kuyobora uwo muryango, uzakoreshwa mu gushaka uzasimbura no gukemura ibibazo byatumye ibihugu binanirwa kumvikana.

Mushikiwabo azakomeza imirimo yari asanzwe ashinzwe, harimo no gukurikirana ivugururwa ry’imikorere y’uyu muryango.

Mu rwego rwa dipolomasi, iyi ni intsinzi y’agateganyo kuko Mushikiwabo yakomeje kugumana umwanya, kandi hatabayeho kumutsinda mu matora cyangwa kumukuraho ku buyobozi. Nubwo atari intsinzi yuzuye, kuko atabonye manda ya gatatu y’imyaka ine yahataniraga, kandi u Rwanda rukaba rutazongera gutanga umukandida kuri uwo mwanya.

Mushikiwabo yagaragaje ko abona iki cyemezo nk’intsinzi ya Afurika, kuko uyu mugabane ufite uruhare runini muri OIF.

Abasesenguzi muri Politiki mpuzamahanga basanga OIF, ibyabaye byo gusubika amatora bigaragaza ko uyu muryango umaze kugera aharindimuka.

Mu kiganiro yagiranye na Kigali Today, umunyamategeko akaba n’umusesenguzi muri Politike Mpuzamahanga, Aloys Mutabingwa, avua ko kuba ibihugu bibiri ari byo bikomye amatora adakorwa nkuko byari biteganyijwe, biteye isoni.

Yagize ati “Niba ari amatora koko cyangwa uburyo bwashyizweho bukaba bwaremejwe buri mw'itegeko, ibyo bihugu bibiri byabaye nk’ibidashaka kubikozwa, dore ko iyo hatabayeho ubwimvikane rusange (Consensus) baratora bisanzwe hakabaho ubwiganze bw’amajwi asanzwe (Simple Majority). Ariko byumvikane nanone ko habayeho ubushishozi burenze ubwakoreshejwe mu gushyiraho ubwo buryo bwo gushaka umunyamabanga mukuru, mu rwego rwo kubungabunga ubumwe bw’abagize uyu muryango.”

Ngo kudakoresha uburyo bwo gutora hakarebwa ubwiganze bw’amajwi, byatumye hatabaho abanyamuryango bashobora gusigarana ingingimira ku mikorere y’umunyamabanga mukuru watowe.

Mutabingwa ati “Icyagaragaraga ni uko Louise Mushikiwabo yashoboraga kubatsinda ariko akamara iyi manda ya gatatu abangamiwe cyane, n’abo batamutoye. Urumva ko hajemo n’iterabwoba bwa RDC yavugaga ngo iravamo, naramuka atowe. Macron na we akumva kuvamo kwa RDC ari ugusenyuka k’umuryango wenda kubera umubare w’abavuga igifaransa uri muri RDC.”

Mutabingwa ati “Byabaye nta wabishidikanya, ahubwo ibisigaye gukorerwa muri uyu mwaka wongerewe manda, ni ukugabanya ubukana bw’iryo hungabana. Ntabwo nzi niba nabyo biri bukoreke kuko ikibazo gikomeye ni ukuba ahantu hakeneye dipulomasi, hari ibihugu bitayishaka. Bishaka gukoresha igitugu n’agahato by’umwihariko RDC n’Ubufaransa. Ndetse ibyo bigahangayikisha ibihugu byo muri Aziya, nemeranya nabyo, bivuga biti kubera iki tugomba kuvanga ibintu bitavangika.”

Ibyo bihugu bisanga ibibazo biri hagati y’igihugu n’ikindi bidakwiye kujya kwivanga mu muryango wose, kubera ko bishobora kuzatuma bimwe mu bihugu bihagarika kuba ibinyamuryango bya OIF mu gihe cyose ibyo bisa n’akajagari byaba bikomeje.

Mutabingwa ati “Ibidashaka kujya mu kajagari bishobora guhagarika kuba abanyamuryango by’agateganyo. Mbibutse ko no kugera aho u Rwanda ruhabwa kuyobora uyu muryango, byari mu rwego rwo kugarura ubwumvikane n’umubano wari umaze igihe kirekire urimo igatotsi gakomeye kuva mu gihe cya Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu 1994. Ntabwo ari ibintu byitwa ko bigendera ku bushake bw’Ubufaransa na Canada.”

Ngo ni Ubufaransa bwashakaga kugaragaza ko bwahinduye umujyo, bukaba butakiri muri ya mateka mabi yo guhangana n’ubutegetsi bw’u Rwanda, bitewe no kuba Jenoside yabaye mu Rwanda bwarayigizemo uruhare, kandi ikaba itararangiye nkuko abayiteguye babishakaga.

Absesenguzi kandi basanga OIF ikeneye u Rwanda nkuko na rwo ruyikeneye, kubera ko ibintu ari magirirane, kandi rukaba rukwiye guhabwa uburenganzira bungana n’ubw’ibindi bihugu, ntihagire ibitoneshwa ngo ibindi bitsikamirwe.

Mutabingwa ati “Ni ikibazo cy’ubwubahane ndetse no kurindana ibintu bituma ayari amakimbirane hagati y’abanyamuryango babiri, ahinduka aya rusange mu muryango. Hakabaho abantu n’udutsiko bagerageza kurindana. Ibyo bintu uwabigizemo uruhare wa mbere ni Ubufaransa. Ntabwo jye ikibazo mfite ari icyo RDC kuba yakwitwara uko yitwaye, ikibazo mfite ni umuntu ugererageza kugira uruhande ahagararamo kandi ari we wari ukwiye guhagarara hagati.”

Iki kibazo ngo Ubufaransa butakitondeye, kubera ko iyi ari imiryango yubakiye kuri dipulomasi hari ubwo ibintu byasubira irudubi, kubera ko kuba u Rwanda rutazongera kwiyamamaza ari uko rutishimiye iyo myitwarire, ku buryo rushobora no kuva muri uwo muryango rugakomezanya n’ibindi.

The Estonian government says it will shut the crossings after accusing Russia of directing an alleged sabotage attack on a drone manufacturer

Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe".

The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian.

They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids.

On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries.

The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website.

Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia".

Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage.

The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media.

Estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with Russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions.

One of them is located at Narva, Estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border.

Kremlin spokesman Dimitry Peskov said: "Estonia is building a wall. Many countries, as history demonstrates, have built walls that have brought nothing good to those who erect such walls."

Russia has been repeatedly accused by European leaders of targeting national infrastructure and resources destined for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Baltic region leaders have repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid attacks and raised fears about the Kremlin's territorial ambitions.

Other major backers of Ukraine in Europe, including France, Germany, the UK and Poland, have also said Russia has orchestrated attacks on their soil in recent months.

Last year, six men were jailed in the UK over an arson attack linked to Russia at a London warehouse where aid bound for Ukraine was being stored.
